topology: SRV1 192.168.10.10/24 — R1 Gi0/0 192.168.10.1/24; R1 Gi0/1 203.0.113.1/24 — ISP1 Gi0/0 203.0.113.2/24; ISP1 Gi0/1 198.51.100.1/24 — PC1 198.51.100.10/24. Both hosts have gateways. SRV1 serves the prepared HTTP page; ISP1 has no route to the private LAN.
verificationNotes: Practice starts at zero credit with addressing, ISP1 and HTTP ready. R1 has no NAT roles, mapping or default. The completed reference applies only published R1 commands and earns four configuration goals; two real translated pings and one delivered HTTP response are required for all seven tasks.

Static NAT maps the entire inside local address 192.168.10.10 to the inside global address 203.0.113.10. The public alias is unassigned to physical interfaces; R1 answers ISP1 ARP on its outside interface. No NAT allocation ACL, pool or overload is needed.

Translated ICMP achievements correlate the actual NAT router event, delivered request packet identity and successful translated return. Router-originated probes, untranslated private reachability, a permanent static row or aggregate hit counters cannot fabricate them.

HTTP credit requires a corresponding TCP transaction at PC1 and SRV1, a completed 200 response with the actual page content and NAT events matching its endpoint ports. A wrong path, disabled service, missing returned data, SYN or ICMP success cannot finish that task.

Each missing role, wrong inside mapping and missing default is exercised. A partial configuration can return ICMP from an untranslated private address; it does not prove the intended public mapping. R1’s default is separate from NAT. NAT is not a firewall.
Clearing dynamic NAT state preserves the permanent static entry. Active static deletion uses IOS confirmation or prior child-flow clearing. Fresh traffic recreates real protocol entries.
Packet achievements survive portable saves and browser reopening, while current NAT roles, static mapping and usable upstream route remain live. Reopening rebuilds fresh runtime state.

The lab uses the existing simulated IPv4 NAT, ARP, routing, ICMP, TCP and HTTP implementations. It does not claim new live CML validation and does not add PAT, port forwarding, outside source NAT or firewall policy.
